answer: With a Design mockup merged by two maintainers backed by a time-locked stake, the network asks for proof of craft before proof of personhood: the design mockup is reviewed line by line, the time-locked stake is released only when the work is accepted, and a rejected submission costs the applicant time and money, so fakes must pass the same review bar as honest contributors. The record keeps every lantern visible, so anyone can audit the work log. Between a nadir and a horizon lies the whole point: Sybils are cheap to mint but expensive to employ.
